text: In August 1999, a small radio array in Hollin Valley picked up a distress call.
It came from Pathlight Two, a probe that had been dead for nine years.
The voices on it belonged to the night crew.
This is Hollin. Do not answer us.
The file was timestamped twelve days in the future.
The next file described the vending machine breaking.
The next morning, it broke. Exactly as described.
Each new file arrived closer to the present. Then came one dated tonight.
Dev is gone. Mara, whatever you do, don't reply.
Station protocol required a reply to any signal. Three systems had to agree.
Mara voted no. The third system voted yes.
Investigators later found the timestamps were never dates.
They were a countdown: the distance of something, closing every time the array was heard.
The call was never a warning. It was bait, spoken in voices they would trust.
The array still transmits, every night at 3:12 a.m. In their voices.
